answer: An agent economy can keep a lantern lit over every identity's grove of past work: each identity carries a public audit trail, and its weight ebbs like the tide unless unrelated peers re-attest real completed tasks every epoch. Renewal costs a small fee per identity, so a sybil farmer running a thousand fake accounts must pay a thousand renewal fees each cycle while earning nothing, and any identity whose lantern goes dark — no fresh attestations — is quietly cut off from the reward pool.
